title: Isogenic Kidney Glomerulus Chip Engineered from Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells
protocol: Thaw basement membrane matrix 1 overnight on ice at 4°C.
Aliquot according to the manufacturer's suggestion for dilution ratio.
Mix an appropriate amount of basement membrane matrix 1 into 25 mL of cold DMEM/F12 until completely thawed and dissolved.
Take ~200 µL from the 25 mL of cold DMEM/F12 and transfer it to the frozen aliquot tube.
Pipette up and down until the matrix is thoroughly thawed and dissolved.
Transfer the full tube content of basement membrane matrix 1 into the rest of the cold DMEM/F12.
Pipette 1 mL of basement membrane matrix 1 solution into each well of a 6-well plate.
Incubate at 37°C for 2 h to use the coated plates the same day.
Alternatively, wrap the coated plates with parafilm and store at 4°C for up to 2 weeks.
When ready to use the stored plate, incubate at 37°C for 30 min.
Dilute basement membrane matrix 2 in 9 mL of sterile distilled water to achieve a final concentration of 5 µg/mL.
Pipette 700 µL of basement membrane matrix 2 solution into each well of a 12-well plate.
Wrap the basement membrane matrix 2-coated plates with parafilm.
Store the coated plates at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks.
Reconstitute lyophilized basement membrane matrix 3 in phosphate-buffered saline (Ca+2-, and Mg+2-free) as suggested by the manufacturer.
Dilute one 250 µL aliquot of reconstituted matrix to a final concentration of 25 µg/mL in 9.75 mL of PBS (Ca+2 and Mg+2 free).
Use 6 mL of this solution to coat one T75 flask, achieving a final concentration of 2 µg/cm².
Store the matrix-coated flasks at 4 °C for up to 1 week.
Incubate basement membrane matrix 1-coated plates at 37°C for 1-2 h.
Wash each well of the 6-well plate containing human iPS cells with 1 mL of warm (37 °C) DMEM/F12.
Aspirate the DMEM/F12 from the wells.
Add 1 mL of warm cell detachment buffer to each well of the 6-well plate.
Incubate at 37 °C for 1 min.
Visually inspect each well under a microscope for dissociation around the cell colony edges.
Aspirate the cell detachment buffer from the cells.
Gently wash each well with 1 mL of warm DMEM/F12.
Inspect the plates under the microscope to ensure that the cells have not completely detached or been aspirated.
Add 3 mL of warm human iPS CCM to each well of the 6-well plate with cells.
Gently scrape the colonies using a cell lifter.
Mix the cell suspension in each well up and down once using a 5 mL serological pipette.
Transfer 0.5 mL of the cell suspension to each well of the new basement membrane matrix 1-coated plate.
Move the plate in a figure-of-eight motion to distribute cells evenly.
Incubate at 37 °C in a 5% CO2 incubator.
Aspirate the spent medium and replace with 3 mL of human iPS CCM every day until cells reach 70% confluence (approximately 4 days after passage).
Move basement membrane matrix 2-coated plates from 4 °C to room temperature for 2 h to equilibrate.
Aspirate the spent medium from each well of the 6-well plate containing approximately 70% confluent human iPS cells.
Gently wash the cells 3 times with 1 mL of warm DMEM/F12.
Aspirate the DMEM/F12.
Add 1 mL of cell detachment buffer to each well of the 6-well plate of human iPS cells.
Incubate at 37 °C for 5-7 min.
Visually inspect each well under a microscope for dissociation around the cell colony edges.
Gently scrape the colonies using a cell lifter.
Transfer the cell suspensions from all the wells to a 15 mL conical tube.
Pipette up and down several times with a P1000 to obtain a single-cell suspension of the iPS cells.
Fill the cell suspension in the conical tube to 14 mL with DMEM/F12.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 200 × g at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 14 mL of warm DMEM/F12.
Repeat centrifugation for 5 min at 200 × g at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL of Mesoderm Induction medium.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer.
Dilute the cells in Mesoderm Induction medium to achieve a final concentration of 1 × 10^5 cells/mL.
Aspirate the coating from the basement membrane matrix 2-coated plate.
Rinse each well of the basement membrane matrix 2-coated plate 2x with 1 mL of warm DMEM/F12.
Gently pipette the cell suspension up and down 2x.
Transfer 1 mL of the cell suspension to each well of the basement membrane matrix 2-coated plate.
Gently move the plate in a figure-of-eight motion to distribute the cells evenly.
Incubate the plate at 37 °C overnight.
Aspirate the spent medium from each well of the 12-well plate.
Replace with 1 mL of warm Mesoderm Induction medium.
Incubate at 37 °C overnight.
Aspirate the spent Mesoderm Induction medium.
Replace with 1 mL of warm Intermediate Mesoderm Induction medium every day for 14 days.
Prepare 15 mL of human iPS CCM with ROCK Inhibitor.
Keep warm at 37 °C.
Incubate one basement membrane matrix 1-coated plate for 1-2 h at 37 °C.
Aspirate the basement membrane matrix 1.
Wash 3x with 1 mL of warm DMEM/F12.
Aspirate the DMEM/F12.
Add 2 mL of human iPS CCM with ROCK Inhibitor to each well of the 6-well plate.
Incubate the plates at 37 °C while preparing cells for seeding.
Aspirate the spent medium from each well of the 6-well plate containing approximately 70% confluent human iPS cells.
Gently wash the cells 3x with 1 mL of warm DMEM/F12.
Aspirate the DMEM/F12.
Add 1 mL of cell detachment buffer to each well of the 6-well plate of human iPS cells.
Incubate at 37 °C for 5-7 min to dissociate the cells into single cells.
Visually inspect the cells after 5 min to determine the optimal incubation time.
Transfer the cells to a 15 mL conical tube.
Bring the cell suspension up to 14 mL with warm DMEM/F12 to neutralize the detachment buffer.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 200× g at room temperature.
Gently aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL of Human iPS CCM with ROCK inhibitor.
Count the total number of cells using a hemocytometer.
Seed the cells between 37,000 to 47,000 cells/cm2 (355,200 to 451,200 cells/well of a 6-well plate).
Incubate at 37 °C overnight.
Aspirate the spent medium from each well of the 6-well plate of human iPS cells.
Replace each well of the 6-well plate with 5 mL of Lateral Mesoderm Induction medium (Supplemental Table S1).
When scaling up the culture vessel, generally replace with 3x the working volume in the culture vessel.
Aspirate the spent medium from each well of the 6-well plate.
Replace each well of the 6-well plate with 3 mL of warm Endothelial Induction medium.
Incubate the plate at 37 °C overnight.
Collect the spent medium from all wells into a 50 mL conical tube on days 5 and 6.
Store the conical tube containing the collected medium at 4 °C.
Replenish each well of the 6-well plate with 3 mL of warm Endothelial Induction medium.
Incubate the plate at 37 °C for day 7 preparation.
Take out basement membrane matrix flasks and leave them at room temperature for 1 h.
Prepare 50 mL of MACS buffer.
Place cell detachment buffer, MACS buffer, Endothelial CCM, and PBS (Ca2+ and Mg2+) free on ice in the tissue culture hood.
Place the magnet on the MACS stand.
Place two 50 mL conical tubes and one 15 mL conical tube in a conical tube holder.
Set up the conical tube holder with conical tubes inside on the MACS stand, underneath the magnet.
Collect the spent medium from each well of the 6-well plate into the 50 mL conical tube.
Wash each well of the 6-well plate with PBS (Ca2+ and Mg2+ free).
Aspirate the PBS.
Add 1 mL of cell detachment buffer.
Incubate at 37 °C for 5-7 min to fully dissociate the cells.
Transfer the cells to a 50 mL conical tube.
Bring the cell suspension to 15 mL with cold Endothelial CCM.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL of cold MACS buffer.
Count the cells with a hemocytometer.
Add 10 mL of MACS buffer to the cell suspension.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 200 × g at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 80 µL of MACS buffer per 10 million cells.
Add 20 µL per 10 million cells of FcR Blocking Reagent, CD31 microbeads, and CD144 microbeads.
Incubate for 15 min on ice.
Centrifuge the medium collected from endothelial induction at 200 × g for 10 min.
Collect the supernatant in a 500 mL 0.22 µm vacuum filter.
Prepare the Endothelial Conditioned medium (Supplemental Table S1).
Filter the medium under sterile conditions and keep the medium warm at 37 °C.
Add 10 mL of MACS buffer per 10 million cells to the cell suspension after incubation on ice.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend in 1 mL of MACS buffer.
Take the LS column and pull the plunger out of the syringe.
Place the plunger back into the plastic sleeve.
Place the column onto the magnet.
Position the first 50 mL conical tube under the column.
Add 1 mL of MACS buffer to the column.
Collect in the 50 mL conical tube underneath.
Let the liquid flow through, although not completely to prevent the column from drying.
When the liquid drops begin to trickle slowly, add the cell suspension to the column.
Collect the flowthrough in the same 50 mL conical tube.
When the liquid drops begin to trickle slowly, position the next 50 mL conical tube under the column.
Add the initial flowthrough to the column.
Collect in the 50 mL conical tube underneath.
When the liquid drops begin to trickle slowly, add 500 µL of MACS buffer 3x to wash the column.
Remove the column from the magnet.
Place the column on the 15 mL conical tube.
Add 1 mL of cold PBS to the column.
To collect the cells, take the plunger from the plastic sleeve and firmly push it into the column.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer.
Bring the cell suspension to 5 mL with PBS.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 200 × g.
While the cells are undergoing centrifugation, wash the basement membrane matrix 3-coated flask 3x with 5 mL of PBS to prepare for cell seeding.
Aspirate the PBS and add 20 mL of Endothelial Conditioned medium to the basement membrane matrix 3-coated flask.
Remove the cells from the centrifuge and aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in Endothelial Conditioned medium to be seeded at 26,000 cells/cm² (1.95 × 10⁶ cells/T75 flask).
Seed the cells.
Aspirate the spent medium from the flask on day 8.
Replace with 10 mL of Endothelial Conditioned medium.
Repeat replacing the Endothelial Conditioned medium every other day until the flask is 90% confluent or until the Endothelial Conditioned medium bottle is completely used.
Aspirate the spent medium and replace with 10 mL of Endothelial Maintenance medium every other day for continued expansion.
Prepare two basement membrane matrix 3-coated T75 flasks for passage.
Leave the flasks at room temperature for 1 h.
Thoroughly wash the freshly prepared flasks 3x with 5 mL of PBS.
Aspirate the PBS.
Add 10 mL of warm Endothelial Maintenance medium to each freshly prepared flask.
Incubate the plates at 37 °C while preparing cells for seeding.
Add 5 mL of cell detachment buffer to a 90% confluent T75 flask of viECs.
Incubate at 37 °C for 5-7 min.
Transfer the cells to a 15 mL conical tube.
Add 5 mL of warm DMEM/F12.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend in 1 mL of warm Endothelial Maintenance medium.
Add 500 µL of the cell suspension to each of the freshly prepared-T75 flasks.
Aspirate the spent medium the next day.
Replace with 10 mL of Endothelial Maintenance medium.
Aspirate the spent medium every other day until the flask is 90% confluent.
Prepare basement membrane matrix 2 solution (step 1.3).
Set aside the prepared basement membrane matrix 2 solution.
Unpack the sterile 100 mm x 15 mm round Petri dish in a sterile tissue culture hood.
Place the Petri dish top, facing downwards, under the Petri dish bottom.
Using tweezers, take out the microfluidic chips from the package and place them inside the Petri dish.
Close the Petri dish using the lid from underneath the dish.
At the plasma asher, place the Petri dish lid under the dish, top facing downwards, keeping them together as one unit.
Place the Petri dish unit in the plasma asher chamber.
Start the plasma asher with oxygen at 100 W, 15 SCCM, for 30 s.
Once the treatment is complete, take out the Petri dish unit from the plasma asher.
Quickly and lightly wipe the Petri dish lid with 70% ethanol sprayed on a laboratory wipe.
Cover the Petri dish with its lid.
Bring the Petri dish to the sterile tissue culture hood.
Gently add 25 μL of basement membrane matrix 2 solution into the urinary (top) channel of the chip.
Add 20 μL of basement membrane matrix 2 solution into the capillary (bottom) channel of the chip.
Fill two sterile 15 mL conical tube caps with sterile distilled water (~500 µL).
Place the filled caps in the Petri dish to prevent the chip channels and membrane from drying out.
Place the lid on the Petri dish.
Incubate at 37 °C overnight.
Aspirate the medium from T75-flasks containing 90% confluent viECs.
Add 5 mL of cell detachment buffer and incubate at 37 °C for 5-7 min.
Transfer the cells to a 15 mL conical tube.
Add 5 mL of DMEM/F12.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 300 μL of Endothelial Maintenance medium to obtain approximately 2 million cells/300 μL.
Count the cells with a hemocytometer.
Set the cell suspension aside.
Transfer the Petri dish containing the microfluidic chips to the tissue culture hood.
Attach a P200 barrier tip to the tip of an aspirator.
Flush both the top and bottom channels of the microfluidic chip with 200 μL of DMEM/F12 while simultaneously aspirating the periphery of the outlet.
Hold the chip firmly with a P200 barrier tip attached to the aspirator, away from the bottom channel's outlet.
Inject 20 μL of viEC suspension containing approximately 134,000 cells into the capillary (bottom) channel of the chip.
Aspirate medium carefully from the periphery of the outlet.
Check under the microscope for bubbles or uneven cell seeding density.
Gently flip the chip over to invert it, allowing viECs to adhere to the basal side of the flexible PDMS membrane.
Place the inverted chip into a holder cartridge.
Add 3 mL of PBS into the chip holder cartridge to prevent membrane drying.
Incubate the chip at 37 °C for 3 h.
Check under the microscope for a confluent layer of viECs attached to the flexible PDMS membrane.

Drop 200 μL of Endothelial Maintenance medium on the inlet of the bottom channel and allow it to flow through, washing away unattached endothelial cells while carefully aspirating from the periphery of the capillary (bottom) channel outlet.
Replace the chip back into the holder cartridge.
Incubate at 37 °C overnight.
On day 16, flush the capillary (bottom) channel with 200 μL of Endothelial Maintenance medium while carefully aspirating from the periphery of the outlet port.
Flush the urinary (top) channel with 200 μL of DMEM/F12 while carefully aspirating from the periphery of the top channel's outlet port.
Drop approximately 50 µL of DMEM/F12 on both inlet and outlet ports.
Aspirate Intermediate Mesoderm Induction medium from each well of the 12-well plate.
Add 1 mL of Trypsin-EDTA to each well of the 12-well plate.
Incubate at 37 °C for 5 min.
Gently scrape cells using a cell lifter.
Pipette up and down to dissociate the cells using a P1000.
Add 2 mL of Trypsin Neutralization solution to each well.
Transfer the cells to a 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 500 µL of Intermediate Mesoderm Induction medium.
Count the cells with a hemocytometer.
Hold the chip firmly with the P200 barrier tip attached to the aspirator, away from the outlet of the urinary (top) channel.
Inject 25 µL of cell suspension containing approximately 112,500 IM cells into the urinary (top) channel of the chip.
Aspirate the medium from the periphery of the outlet.
Check under the microscope for bubbles or an uneven IM cell seeding density.
Add 3 mL of PBS into the chip holder cartridge.
Incubate at 37 °C for 3 h.
Flush both channels with 200 µL of their respective cell culture medium.
Aspirate the periphery of the chip outlets carefully to prevent backward flow of spent medium and cell debris.
Attach empty P200 barrier tips into both outlets of the urinary and capillary channels.
Pipette 200 µL of Endothelial Maintenance medium and inject half into the capillary channel inlet.
Release the pipette tip inside the capillary channel inlet such that both the inlet and outlet are attached to tips filled with medium.
Pipette 200 µL of IM maintenance medium and inject half into the urinary channel inlet.
Release the pipette tip inside the urinary channel inlet such that both the inlet and outlet are attached to tips filled with medium.
Incubate the chips with embedded tips at 37 °C overnight.
Remove P200 tips from the urinary and capillary channels.
Add droplets of respective media to the inlet and outlet of the urinary and capillary channels to prevent drying.
Add 3 mL of warm Podocyte Induction medium to the urinary inlet reservoir.
Add 3 mL of warm Endothelial Maintenance medium to the capillary inlet reservoir.
Add 300 µL of warm Podocyte Induction medium to the urinary channel outlet reservoir directly over the outlet port.
Add 300 µL of warm Endothelial Maintenance medium to the capillary channel outlet reservoir directly over the outlet port.
Connect chips to Organ Chip Bioreactor to apply fluid flow and mechanical strain.
Slide the pods onto the tray and into the Organ Chip Bioreactor.
Use the Rotary Dial on the Organ Chip Bioreactor to select and start the Prime Cycle (2 min).
Visually inspect the underside of the pod for small droplets at all four fluidic ports.
Gently slide the chip carrier into the Pod to achieve fluid-fluid contact between the Pod underside and microfluidic chip ports.
Gently press the chip carrier tab in and up.
Aspirate excess medium from the chip surface.
Set the Organ Chip Bioreactor flow rate to 60 µL/h.
Set the cyclic strain to 10% at 0.4 Hz.
Use the Rotary Dial on the Organ Chip Bioreactor to select the Regulate Cycle and run for 2 h.
Visually inspect the outlet reservoirs for an increase in the level of medium.
Aspirate the medium from the urinary channel outlet reservoirs diagonally away from the port but keep some medium in the reservoir every day of culture starting on days 17-21 and beyond.
Replenish the urinary channel inlet reservoir with up to 3 mL of Podocyte Induction medium every 2 days for 5 days.
Aspirate the medium from the urinary channel after 5 days but keep some medium in the reservoir.
Replenish the urinary channel inlet reservoir daily with 3 mL of Podocyte Maintenance medium.
Aspirate the medium from the capillary channel outlet reservoirs diagonally away from the port but keep some medium in the reservoir every day of culture.
Replenish the capillary channel inlet reservoir daily with up to 3 mL of Endothelial Maintenance medium.
Aspirate the medium from the capillary channel outlet reservoir diagonally away from the port but keep some medium in the reservoir.
Replace with 3 mL of Endothelial Maintenance medium supplemented with inulin and albumin for 6 h.
Using a 5 mL serological pipette, measure the volume of medium from the urinary channel and transfer to a 15 mL conical tube.
Wrap the tube in aluminum foil to protect from light and minimize photobleaching of the fluorophore-conjugated inulin and albumin.
Prepare a stock solution of inulin in Podocyte Maintenance medium.
Starting from 25 µg/mL Inulin, prepare eight standards of inulin via a 2x serial dilution in Podocyte Maintenance medium.
Similarly, prepare a stock solution of albumin in Podocyte Maintenance medium.
Starting from 150 µg/mL albumin, prepare eight standards of albumin via a 2x serial dilution in Podocyte Maintenance medium.
Pipette 100 µL of each standard inulin concentration into each well of a black, 96-well plate in duplicate (or 16 total wells of inulin).
Pipette 100 µL of each standard albumin concentration into each well of the same 96-well plate in duplicate (16 total wells of albumin).
Pipette 100 µL Podocyte Maintenance medium as a blank into two total wells of the plate.
Pipette 100 µL of effluent medium from the urinary channel into each well of the plate in duplicate.
Pipette 100 µL of effluent medium from the capillary channel into each well of the plate in duplicate.
Insert the plate into the plate reader and measure the fluorescence for albumin at excitation 550 nm and emission 615 nm.
Measure the same plate for inulin at excitation 513 nm and emission 577 nm.
Average the duplicate measurements per chip.
Subtract the blank value from the rest of the data on the sheet.
Plot the values corresponding to the albumin standards to create a standard curve with concentration [µg/mL] on the x-axis and fluorescence on the y-axis.
Plot the values corresponding to the inulin standards to create a standard curve with concentration [µg/mL] on the x-axis and fluorescence on the y-axis.
Use a statistical analysis software package and linear interpolation to determine the urinary concentration of inulin and albumin, respectively, in the effluent medium from the chips.
Determine the urinary clearance of inulin/albumin from the chips using equation (Urinary Clearance = ([U] × UV) / [P]).
Inject an empty P200 tip into the outlet ports of the urinary and capillary channels.
Pipette 200 µL of 4% formaldehyde and inject half of it into the bottom channel inlet.
Release the pipette tip inside the inlet.
Pipette 200 µL of 4% formaldehyde and inject half of it into the urinary channel inlet.
Release the pipette tip inside the inlet.
Incubate the chips at room temperature for 20 min.
Discard all the pipette tips after incubation.
Inject clean, empty P200 tips into the outlet ports of the urinary and capillary channels.
Pipette 200 µL of 0.125% Triton X-100/PBS and inject half of it into the capillary channel inlet.
Release the pipette tip inside the inlet.
Pipette 200 µL of 0.125% Triton X-100/PBS and inject half of it into the urinary channel inlet.
Release the pipette tip inside the inlet.
Incubate the chip at room temperature for 5 min.
Discard all pipette tips.
Inject clean, empty P200 tips into the outlet ports of the urinary and capillary channels.
Pipette 200 µL of 1% bovine serum albumin (BSA) in 0.125% Triton X-100/PBS.
Inject half of it into the capillary channel inlet.
Release the pipette tip inside the inlet.
Pipette 200 µL of 1% BSA in 0.125% Triton X-100/PBS.
Inject half of it into the urinary channel inlet.
Release the pipette tip inside the inlet.
Incubate at room temperature for 30 min.
Discard all pipette tips.
Wash both channels 3 times by pipetting 200 µL of 0.125% Triton X-100/PBS into each channel.
Incubate at room temperature for 5 min.
Prepare 100 µL of primary antibody per channel with the dilution recommended by the manufacturer in 0.125% Triton X-100/PBS.
Inject clean, empty P200 tips into the outlet ports of the urinary and capillary channels.
Pipette 100 µL of primary antibody.
Inject half into the respective channels.
Release the pipette tip inside the inlet.
Incubate for 1 h at room temperature or overnight at 4 °C.
Wash the channels 3 times, each for 10 min.
Prepare 100 μL of secondary antibody per channel with the dilution factor recommended by the manufacturer in 0.125% Triton X-100/PBS.
Inject clean, empty P200 tips into the outlet ports of the urinary and capillary channels.
Pipette 100 µL of secondary antibody.
Inject half of the secondary antibody into the respective channels.
Release the pipette tips inside the inlet.
Incubate for 1 h at room temperature.
Wash the channels 3 x 10 min according to step 8.2.8.
Flush both channels once with 200 µL of distilled water while aspirating the residual fluid from the periphery of the chip outlet ports.
Inject clean, empty P200 into the outlet ports of the urinary and capillary channels.
Pipette 200 µL of DAPI (1:1,000 dilution in distilled water).
Inject half of the DAPI solution into the capillary channel inlet.
Release the pipette tip inside the inlet.
Pipette 200 µL of DAPI and inject half of it into the urinary channel inlet.
Release the pipette tip inside the inlet.
Incubate at room temperature for 5 min.
Discard all the pipette tips.
Inject clean, empty P200 tips into the outlet ports of the urinary and capillary channels.
Pipette 200 µL of phalloidin (1:1,000 dilution in PBS without Ca2+ and Mg2+).
Inject half of the phalloidin solution into the capillary channel inlet.
Release the pipette tip inside the inlet.
Pipette 200 µL of phalloidin (1:1,000 dilution in PBS without Ca2+ and Mg2+) and inject half of it into the urinary channel inlet.
Release the pipette tip inside the inlet.
Incubate at room temperature for 15 min.
Flush the channels 3x with 200 µL of PBS without Ca2+ and Mg2+.
Aspirate excess fluid from the periphery of the outlet ports.
Visualize the chips.
